name: mris_preproc
purpose: Prepare surface-based data for high-level analysis by resampling surface or volume source data to a common subject (usually an average subject) and concatenating them into one file usable by programs such as mri_glmfit.

inputs.statement: With --meas surfmeasure, input is taken from subject/surf/hemi.surfmeasure.
The --fsgd option specifies the input subject list from an FSGD file.
inputs.quote:
--fsgd fsgdfile
Specify the list of input subjects from the fsgd file.

inputs.statement: The registration matrix file is of the type accepted or created by tkregister2.
inputs.quote: The registration matrix file is of the type accepted/created by tkregister2.

inputs.statement: The --target option selects the common-space subject; --hemi selects lh or rh for source and target surfaces.
inputs.quote:
--target subject
Subject to use as the common-space. All the input data will be resampled to the surface of this subject.
--hemi hemi
Use hemi for source and target surfaces. hemi can be lh or rh.

conditions.statement: When subjects are listed using --s, each has its own --s; this option is for use with --meas.
conditions.quote:
--s subjN
Specify an input subject on the command-line. All subjects must be specified in this way on the command-line (ie, each with its own --s). For use with --meas.

conditions.statement: The --is option is an alternative to --meas and still requires a supplied subject list.
conditions.quote:
--is surfmeasfile
Specify full path to input surface measure file. This is an alternative to using --meas. This still requires that a subject list be supplied.

conditions.statement: For --paired-diff there must be an even number of inputs.
conditions.quote:
--paired-diff
After concatenating all the inputs together, create a new output file by computing paired differences, ie, Input1-Input2, Input3-Input4, etc. There must be an even number of inputs.

conditions.statement: When using full paths with --fsgd, subjects must be in the same order as the input surface files.
conditions.quote:
Same as #1 but using full paths. Note there is no --meas, but
--fsgd still needed to provide list of subjects, which must be in the same order as the --isp.
If you want to cache without actually creating an output, then --cache-out-only. You must supply a tmpdir.

steps.statement: Surface or volume source data are resampled to a common subject, usually an average subject.
steps.quote: resampling surface or volume source data to a common sujbect (usually an average subject)

steps.statement: Concatenate the resampled inputs into one output file.
steps.quote: Script to prepare surface-based data for high-level analysis by resampling surface or volume source data to a common sujbect (usually an average subject) and then concatenating them into one file

steps.statement: The target surface data may be smoothed by an FWHM specified in millimeters.
steps.quote: Smooth the data on the target surface by fwhm mm.

steps.statement: When sampling a volume, sample a fraction of the thickness along the surface normal.
steps.quote: sample a fraction of the thickness along the surface normal

steps.statement: Optionally compute paired differences after concatenation.
steps.quote: After concatenating all the inputs together, create a new output file by computing paired differences

steps.statement: Optionally compute the mean of all inputs after concatenation and possible paired diffs.
steps.quote: After concatenating all the inputs together (and possibly computing paired diffs), compute the mean of all inputs.

exceptions.statement: ANALYZE and NIFTI formats cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.
exceptions.quote: This will not work for ANALYZE and NIFTI formats because they cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.

exceptions.statement: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.
exceptions.quote: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.

outputs.statement: The --out option specifies the output file.
With caching, per-subject data are saved in the subject's surf directory as hemi.cachefile.
outputs.quote: mris_preproc will save the data for each subject, after resampling to the target and smoothing, in the subjects surf directory as hemi.cachefile.

outputs.statement: Output is a volume-encoded surface file, normally with spatial dimension nvertices-by-1-by-1.
outputs.quote: Normally, the output volume-encoded surface file will have spatial dimension of nvertices-by-1-by-1

parameters.statement: --projfrac sets the projection fraction for vol2surf and is 0-1, default 0.
parameters.quote:
--projfrac projfrac
When sampling a volume onto the surface, sample a fraction of the thickness along the surface normal. projfrac is 0-1. Default is 0.

parameters.statement: The --fwhm option smooths data on the target surface by the specified FWHM in millimeters.
parameters.quote:
--fwhm fwhm
Smooth the data on the target surface by fwhm mm.

parameters.statement: --surfreg sets the surface registration to the common space; default is sphere.reg.
parameters.quote: Use hemi.SurfReg as the surface registration to the common space. Default is sphere.reg.
